```dart

 case TurnStartEvent(): _onTurnStart();

}
```

New dispatch:
```dart
await _agentEventHandlers[event.runtimeType]?.call(this, event, cancelToken);
```

Critical differences to check:

1. **Synchronous vs async handlers**: In the old switch, cases without `await` run SYNCHRONOUSLY (the switch completes before the enclosing async function's first await... well actually the function `_onAgentEvent` is async, and the switch body executes synchronously up to the `await _persistModelRequest` / `await _onAgentEnd()`). In the new version, EVERY handler is invoked via `.call(...)` returning a Future which is then `await`ed. For handlers that were previously sync, this changes the timing: in the old code, `_onAgentStart()` etc. completed before the function returns its future... hmm. Actually in an async function, all code before the first await runs synchronously when called. In the old code, if event is AgentStartEvent, no await is hit, so the entire body (watchdog rearm, trajectory, handler) runs synchronously during the call. In the new code, `_agentEventHandlers[...]?.call(this, event, cancelToken)` — the closures are `async` or `=>` returning Future. For `AgentStartEvent: (service, _, _) async => service._onAgentStart()` — async closure: calling it executes the body synchronously up to its first await — since `_onAgentStart()` is sync, the async closure body `service._onAgentStart()` executes synchronously when `.call` is invoked? An `async` function executes its body synchronously until the first `await`. `service._onAgentStart()` has no await, so the whole body runs synchronously at call time, then the future completes. So the side effects still happen synchronously at dispatch time. Then `await` on an already-completed future yields to the microtask queue — meaning the rest of `_onAgentEvent` (nothing after) resumes later, but there's nothing after. So the sync ordering is preserved for side effects within the handler.

  But note: `MessageUpdateEvent: (service, _, _) async => service._onMessageUpdate(...)` — fine. `ModelRequestEvent: (service, event, _) => service._persistModelRequest(...)` — non-async, returns the future directly, then awaited. Same.

# Review: agent services cluster — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

## Findings

### 1. SUGGESTION — `relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

**Old** (`_onHostEvent` switch, base `59fb4482ce`):
```dart
case 'mail_routed':
  _append(fa_ui.FaChatMessage(role: 'system', content: 'mail from ... routed to session ...'));
  // Paint NOW — _append alone does not notify, ...
  if (!silent) notifyListeners();   // <-- notify #1 (inside the case)
case 'error': ...
case 'debug': ...
}
if (!silent) notifyListeners();     // <-- notify #2 (after the switch, ALL types)
```
**New**: `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` (line 944–955) contains exactly one `if (!silent) notifyListeners();`, and its caller `_onHostStateEvent` does **not** notify after the `mail_routed` case (only the `tool_result`/`status` and `default` arms notify, each once, in their own handlers). Every other event type keeps the identical single post-dispatch notify, but `mail_routed` goes from 2 `notifyListeners()` calls to 1. The double-notify was almost certainly unintentional (a redundant rebuild), so the new behavior is arguably a fix, but it is a literal behavior deviation in a PR claiming zero behavior change — worth a one-line callout in the PR description rather than a rework.

## Verified clean (detailed checks performed)

- **`agent_service_events.dart` (route table)** — Table `_agentEventHandlers` keys: `AgentStartEvent, TurnStartEvent, MessageUpdateEvent, MessageEndEvent, ToolExecutionStartEvent, ToolExecutionEndEvent, ModelRequestEvent, ToolPairingRepairEvent, AgentEndEvent` — exactly the 10 cases of the old switch; unmapped kinds no-op exactly like the old `default: break;`. Bodies are verbatim (field accesses match the old pattern destructuring: `assistantMessageEvent`, `message`, `toolName/args`, `toolName/result/isError`). **Await-semantics preserved**: all handlers except `_persistModelRequest`/`_onAgentEnd` are synchronous `void` (verified signatures in the new file), and those two were the only ones awaited in the old switch; the async lambda wrappers complete synchronously for the void handlers, so no serialization/interleaving change. `_onToolPairingRepair` guard inverted (`isEmpty || session == null → return`) but logically identical, same `unawaited` append + error logging. Pre-dispatch `_armIdleWatchdog()` (skip on AgentEndEvent) and `_trajectory.applyEvent(event)` unchanged.
- **`relay_agent_service.dart` (protocol route table)** — `_protocolMessageHandlers` covers exactly the 10 mapped old cases (`HelloAckMsg, AttachedMsg, MessageDoneMsg, ApprovalRequestMsg, StreamMsg, SettingsResultMsg, ToolsStateMsg, SessionsResultMsg, ExtResultMsg, ErrorMsg`); `ToolsPutMsg` and raw hello frames stay no-ops like the old explicit `break`/`default`. All adapter bodies identical (`unawaited(_decideApproval(...))`, `_sessionsQuery?.complete(...)`, `_error = …; notifyListeners()`). Null-safety identical: casts `message as X` are safe because the map is keyed by exact `runtimeType` (family is `final class`es).
- **`relay_agent_service.dart` (`_onHostEvent` split)** — Outer switch routes exactly `'delta'/'thinking_delta'/'message_done'` to `_onHostStreamEvent` and everything else to `_onHostStateEvent`; `_onHostStateEvent` routes `'tool_result'/'status'` → progress, `'mail_routed'` → mail, default → diagnostics (`'error'`/`'debug'` handled, unknown ignored) — matching old case coverage with no fall-through changes (Dart switch statements don't fall through; shared `tool_result`/`status` arm is fine). `_finishAssistant` decomposition (`_finishAssistantError`/`_finishAssistantContent`/`_finishEmptyAssistant`/`_maybeAutoReauthCodemie`) preserves the exact branch ladder: error-row branch (with its early `return`), tool role, non-assistant roles, empty-assistant (placeholder only when no `toolCalls`), non-empty assistant (append + trajectory record), and the single final `notifyListeners()`.
- **`agent_service_sessions.dart` (loadSession 4-stage split)** — Stage order and every `gen != _loadGeneration` checkpoint preserved (now `return null/false` up to the orchestrator, which returns early exactly where the old code did). The one dropped statement is a *duplicate* consecutive gen-check with no `await` between it and its twin — provably no-op. Phase timings (`storageMs/branchMs/contextMs/ledgerMs`) computed at the same instants; the `AppLog` summary + `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())` run after stage 4 exactly as before. `_reloadExternalMessages` decomposition: windowed ingest reanchored/append branches and full-open re-open preserve all gen checks, the `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` + `_persistedCount` updates, `_growProviderContext` only on plain append, and background refresh on every path that reached it before; the `on Object` torn-read swallow is at the same boundary.
- **`findReusableSession` timezone handling** — Note: it lives in `flutter_session_manager.dart`, not `agent_service_sessions.dart` (the assigned file doesn't contain it). Verified via that file's patch: old `final created = newest.createdAt.toLocal();` + year/month/day compare vs `DateTime.now()` → new `_isToday(newest.createdAt.toLocal())` with the identical y/m/d comparison; the today-check still precedes `_tooLarge` and the user-message scan; unreadable-session fallback still resolves to "do not resume" (`return true` → caller returns null, vs old inner `return null`). **Clean — the claimed toLocal fix is real and no regression was introduced.**
- **`agent_service_history.dart`** — All 188 added lines are verbatim moves from `agent_service.dart`: `_hiddenRecordsResolver` (byte-identical to the old `resolveHiddenRecords` closure, now invoked as `(record) => _hiddenRecordsResolver(reader, record)` — same Future-returning shape), `_historyErrorText` (`e is StateError ? e.message : e.toString()` — matches both old catch sites), `_jumpNewerHistory` chain (jumpToTail → gen check → persist-pass flush → gen check → syncView → applyViewBranch → gen checks → live-rows re-append → `_refreshHistoryAbove` → clear error/notify), and the `jumpToMessage` helpers (`_jumpLoadedTranscript`, `_jumpPositional`, `_pageUntilRowVisible`, `_crawlOlderForRow` with the same `pass < 100 && windowed.hasOlder` loop boundary and `joined.isEmpty || gen != _loadGeneration` stop). Everything else byte-identical to base. All three target part files were already registered (`part 'agent_service_events.dart';` etc. pre-exist in base) and use `part of 'agent_service.dart';`. Loc 2290 < 2800 guard.
- **`agent_tool_availability.dart`** — `_absentToolReason` switch → set+map lookup is behaviorally identical: the four on-device ids have no entry in the static-reason map (no overlap), the guard `onDevice && _onDeviceAbsentTools.contains(id)` reproduces the `when onDevice` guard (off-device media ids fall through to the generic reason exactly as the old wildcard did), and every static reason string is character-identical (`sqlite`, `lsp`, `mcp`, `dap`, `checkpoint`/`rewind` shared, `outlook`). No iteration-order or short-circuit concerns (single dispatch, no loops).

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `agent_service.dart` | ✅ clean (pure 3-hunk delegation) |
| `agent_service_events.dart` | ✅ clean — route table covers exactly the old 10 cases; await semantics preserved (8 sync handlers, 2 previously-awaited async) |
| `agent_service_history.dart` | ✅ clean — verbatim moves; loop boundaries, gen checks, error paths identical |
| `agent_service_sessions.dart` | ✅ clean — staged loadSession/reload preserves all gen guards, phase order, timing points |

| `relay_agent_service.dart` | ⚠️ one SUGGESTION — `mail_routed` loses its historical double-`notifyListeners()` (line 954); all route tables/splits otherwise exactly cover the old case labels and bodies |

**Bottom line: no BLOCKING or IMPORTANT findings in this cluster.** The only deviation found anywhere is the single-notify vs double-notify for `mail_routed` in `relay_agent_service.dart`, which is harmless (one fewer redundant repaint) but should be acknowledged since the PR claims zero behavior change.
